question: When the bidder is following in a trick and holds both the dominant trump and at least one low trump, does playing the low trump cost significant EV (the 'trap'), versus playing the dominant trump?
slice: bidder (P0) following, pip-trump decls (decl_id 0-6), bidder void in led suit or trump led, bidder holds dominant+low trump, oracle-greedy legacy corpus
skip_reason: follow-suit law prevented bidder from playing any trump in those positions
method: Within-snapshot paired contrast: A=play worst low trump, B=play dominant trump. EV delta = Q(B) - Q(A) from oracle E[Q] at decision point. No model query; Q values from corpus snapshot metadata.
